concepts.overview: Steiner assigns the Thrones a formative role in the earliest embodiment. Different accounts ask what they contribute, who receives it, and how it becomes perceptible.
concepts.explanation: GA 110 describes primordial fire substance as the beginning of a world-system plan becoming actual. GA 132 names a receiver for an offering and describes warmth as its outward appearance. The two lectures can be studied together while retaining the question each one answers.
concepts.label: Thrones · Spirits of Will
concepts.open_question: How closely do GA 110’s account of realization, GA 132’s account of the offering, and GA 13’s account of human development describe the same formative operation? The accounts name different recipients and results.

concepts.overview: Cherubim appear as elaborators of an aim, recipients of an offering, and coordinators of planetary motion in distinct accounts.
concepts.explanation: The word “receives” has two different objects here. GA 110 speaks about receiving aims for elaboration. GA 132 speaks about receiving the offering of the Thrones. GA 136 treats the relation of planetary motion to its system.
concepts.label: Cherubim

concepts.overview: In GA 110 the Seraphim receive the aims of a world system from the divine Trinity.
concepts.explanation: GA 110 treats their role at a world-system beginning. GA 136 describes a different activity, spiritual relations among celestial bodies. Keep the initiating source and the field of each activity explicit.
concepts.label: Seraphim

concepts.overview: Steiner’s account distinguishes a capacity developed through Old Saturn from the giving of life in Old Sun.
concepts.explanation: In GA 13, their interaction with Old Saturn develops their capacities. In Old Sun the developing human being receives a life body. GA 132 describes a different gift of wisdom with Archangels as recipients.
concepts.label: Kyriotetes · Spirits of Wisdom

concepts.overview: The spiritual Sun connects several strands of Steiner’s cosmology. The same solar language serves different purposes in the heart analogy and the journey between lives.
concepts.explanation: GA 128 situates the heart and circulation in an inward cosmic image. GA 231 describes a return through the Sun and the formation of a spiritual heart germ. The latter is an event in a spiritual biography, with its own recipient and conditions.
concepts.label: Sun

concepts.overview: Steiner discusses the heart in bodily, symbolic and spiritual-biographical contexts.
concepts.explanation: The heart and circulation take a solar place in GA 128’s inner cosmic picture. GA 231 follows the spiritual germ of a future heart in the account of return to embodiment. Read these as esoteric teachings, with anatomy and physiology addressed separately.
concepts.label: Heart and circulation
concepts.open_question: How should the solar image of circulation, the early disposition of an organ, and the heart germ of a future life be related? The selected passages support separate lines of explanation.

concepts.overview: Old Saturn is the first embodiment in Steiner’s esoteric chronology.
concepts.explanation: GA 110 considers the realization of a world-system aim. GA 132 approaches Old Saturn through offering, warmth and time. GA 13 follows the emergence of the earliest physical disposition. Old Saturn belongs to Steiner’s chronology of embodiments. The present Saturn sphere belongs to a different series.
concepts.label: Old Saturn

concepts.overview: Old Sun is the second embodiment in Steiner’s evolutionary account.
concepts.explanation: GA 13 describes the appearance of actual life in the developing human being. GA 132 describes a gift received by the Archangels that becomes effective later through reflection. The word “Sun” also names a sphere in present spiritual geography.
concepts.label: Old Sun

concepts.overview: Tiphareth is the sixth Sephirah, at the center of the Tree of Life in the Hermetic diagram used as a reference here.
concepts.explanation: The central position provides an entry to solar symbolism in Western Hermetic Qabalah. The Planetary Tree uses this position as an editorial route to Steiner’s Sun dossier. Each tradition retains its own account and source.
concepts.label: Tiphareth
concepts.open_question: What can a comparison of solar symbolism and Steiner’s spiritual Sun illuminate? The relationship shown here establishes a reading route. A fuller comparison needs separate native evidence and a specified function.

concepts.overview: GA 132 follows a specific offering from the Thrones to the Cherubim and describes its appearance as warmth.
concepts.explanation: The passage distinguishes a spiritual activity, its receiver, and the form in which the activity appears to observation. These distinctions guide the comparison with GA 110 and GA 13.
concepts.label: The offering and warmth

lanes.limitation: Read this passage alongside the GA 13 life-body account. The gifts, recipients and stated results differ.
